messages:
sophie.support: Hey - customer on 1.5.2 reporting truncated SSE stream when running on Vercel Edge (edge runtime). They see `ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE` and sometimes duplicated chunk payloads. Billing showed two charges for one request :confused:

kai.eng-runtime: Can you paste the minimal repro and the raw logs? Also which SDK version is used in the app and server?

sophie.support: Repro steps below. App uses `@redwood/inference@1.5.2` (customer thinks 1.6 fixes some streaming bugs but they pinned). Logs: `stream error: ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE at Readable.from (internal/streams) trace=0xabc123ef`. They also saw repeated event bodies like the same chunk arriving twice in one SSE sequence.

sophie.support: Repro code (node 18 on edge-compatible bundler):
```js
// client.js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
const res = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'chat-lite', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hello' }] });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true){
  const { value, done } = await reader.read();
  if(done) break;
  console.log('chunk', new TextDecoder().decode(value));
}
```

and curl against the hosted endpoint shows SSE headers and chunked transfer.

andrew.devex: FYI we had a middleware charset/gzip fix in 1.6 where we normalize `Content-Encoding` and avoid double-transforms on edge bundlers. Could be related if their deploy pipeline inserts another gzip step.

kai.eng-runtime: Two likely causes: 1) token rotation retry happening during stream causing duplicate chunks, 2) edge runtime middleware double-encoding leading to premature stream termination. Can you capture request/response headers and the full raw bytes for one failed run? Need `content-encoding`, `transfer-encoding`, and `content-length` (if present).

sophie.support: Pasted headers from the failing run (sanitized):
```
:method: POST
:path: /v1/chat/stream
host: api.redwood.example
authorization: Bearer ****
content-type: application/sse
content-encoding: gzip
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-rw-sdk-version: 1.5.2
```
They also had a middleware that sets `res.setHeader('Content-Encoding','gzip')` in Next edge function.

kai.eng-runtime: aha. If the edge runtime already gzips, and the runtime pipeline later gzips again or attempts to decompress, you can see duplicate or malformed chunk boundaries. That also explains intermittent duplicate payloads (retries append same chunk).

sophie.support: Customer reported that flipping off their custom gzip middleware fixed the truncation immediately (they tested). But they can't remove it in prod because it's added at platform layer. They asked for a workaround in SDK or server config.

andrew.devex: Short-term: pin SDK to 1.6.0 which has header normalization (we backported a safe check). Long-term: runtime team should tolerate `content-encoding` already set and avoid re-encoding.

kai.eng-runtime: Can you provide trace id and a sample request id? I will check proxies and kernel layering. Trace: `0xabc123ef` request-id `req_2448_0001`. Also please confirm if they use `fetch` polyfill or standard `fetch` on edge. Some polyfills perform their own body transform.

sophie.support: They use `undici` polyfill bundled by their framework. Will ask them to test with native fetch.

devops-bot: Known incident 2026-02-14 "edge gzip double-encode" linked: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2026-02-edge-gzip

kai.eng-runtime: Next steps: (1) recommend customer upgrade SDK to 1.6.0 or apply header normalization wrapper: `if (!res.headersSent) res.removeHeader('Content-Encoding')` before SDK writes; (2) runtime: I'll add a guard to skip re-encoding streaming responses when `content-encoding` present; (3) ops please check proxy (nginx) config for `gzip on` + `proxy_set_header Content-Encoding` double-set.

sophie.support: Customer confirmed SDK 1.6 test passed locally (no truncation). They still want SLA-safe server-side mitigation.

kai.eng-runtime: Assigned to me (kai). I'll drop a small patch and a canary rollout to edge region us-east-1. Tagging @andrew.devex to validate SDK behavior once rollout is live. :thumbsup:

andrew.devex: I'll prepare a docs blurb and a troubleshooting snippet for support (how to detect double-gzip and quick flag to disable middleware).

sophie.support: Thanks team — escalating billing note to finance: they saw duplicate charges for same request id when duplicate chunks were processed. I'll attach the customer billing ids separately. :eyes:

kai.eng-runtime: Will follow up in this thread after canary. For now marking as `escalated-to-runtime`.
